newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Copper prices seen unswayed by Deng's death.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Copper prices seen unswayed by Deng's death.

text.p: Copper prices are unlikely to be swayed by the death of Chinese leader Deng Xiaoping, Australian metal dealers said on Thursday.
China is expected to retain its role as a big importer of copper, which is needed to supplement a shortfall of domestic production, they said.
"China's copper needs are clearly growing and that won't change," said Duncan Cruikshank, metals dealer for BZW Australia.
Copper prices are on an upward trend, partly on the belief that China may buy for its strategic stockpile.
Analysts estimate China will consume about 2.2 million tonnes of copper this year against domestic production of around 900,000 tonnes.
Shanghai copper futures opened up on Thursday despite the death of Deng, firm LME prices giving strong support to the Shanghai market, Chinese copper traders said.
At 0145 GMT, three-month LME copper was fetching about US$2,334-$2339 a tonne, slightly below late U.S. prices.
Deng died in Beijing late on Wednesday of respiratory failure.
